questions.question: Who among the following was a great advocate of English education in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** TB Macaulay.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• English became the official language for the government and courts in 1835, and it was chosen as the official language of teaching. Lord Macaulay was effective in westernizing education in India.
 
• On February 2, 1835, he circulated Minute on Education -- a treatise that offered definitive reasons for why the East India Company and the British government should spend money on the provision of English language education, as well as the promotion of European learning, especially the sciences, in India.
 
• The Minute is based on the idea that English education is not just superior in 'science', but would also inculcate superior morals, etc. that were responsible for making the English superior.
 
• While the Minute acknowledged the historic role of Sanskrit and Arabic literature in the subcontinent, it also contended that they had limitations.
 
• Just about a month after its circulation, the Minute became policy, when William Bentinck (Governor-General of India) got convinced enough to sign the resolution.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Jonathan Duncan:**

 
 
• Jonathan Duncan was Governor of Bombay from 27 December 1795 until his death in 1811.
 
• Lord Cornwallis appointed him superintendent and resident in Benares in 1788, where he worked to put an end to the practice of infanticide.
 
• He was appointed governor of Bombay in 1795 and served in that capacity for the remainder of his life (nearly sixteen years).
 
 
 
• **Warren Hastings:**
 
 
• As the first Governor of the Presidency of Fort William (Bengal), the president of the Supreme Council of Bengal, and consequently the first de facto Governor-General of Bengal from 1772 to 1785, Warren Hastings was a British colonial administrator.
 
• The British Empire in India is said to have been founded by him and Robert Clive.
 
 
 
• **William Jones:**
 
 
• He was a British philologist, a puisne judge on the Supreme Court of Judicature in Fort William, Bengal, and an expert on ancient India.
 
• He is most known for his theory that the Indo-European languages and the European languages share a common ancestor.
 
• In the year 1784, Jones is also credited with founding the Asiatic Society of Bengal.

questions.question: When did the British East India Company start the ‘permanent settlement system’?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1793 CE**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The British East India Company started the **'permanent settlement system' in 1793 CE**.
 
• This system was introduced by **Lord Cornwallis**.
 
• Under this system, the land revenue was fixed permanently, which means it would not be increased in the future.
 
• The zamindars were recognized as the owners of the land, and they had to pay a fixed amount of revenue to the company.
 
• This system aimed to create a loyal and wealthy class of landlords who would support British rule in India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Lord Cornwallis was the **Governor-General of India** from **1786 to 1793**.
 
• The Permanent Settlement covered the provinces of Bengal, Bihar, and Orissa.
 
• While the system aimed at revenue stability, it also led to the exploitation of peasants as zamindars often demanded high rents.
 
• The system had long-term impacts on the agrarian structure and revenue collection in India.

questions.question: In 1600, the East India company acquired a charter from ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Queen Elizabeth I.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **East India Company** was granted a charter by **Queen Elizabeth I** in **1600.**
 
• This charter gave the company a monopoly on **English trade with the East Indies**, which included modern-day** India, Pakistan, Bangladesh, and Indonesia.**
 
• The East India Company played a significant role in **British colonialism and imperialism, **establishing trade relationships and political control over large parts of the Indian subcontinent.
 
• Queen Elizabeth I's charter for the East India Company was a key moment in the history of **British imperialism and global trade**, paving the way for centuries of British economic and political influence in Asia.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **King Edward VI **(reigned 1547-1553) was the **son of Henry VIII **and ruled England for a brief period before his death at the age of 15.
 
• **King Henry IV **(reigned 1399-1413) was the** first monarch **of the House of Lancaster and played a key role in the** English civil war **known as the **Wars of the Roses.**
 
• **Queen Victoria** (reigned 1837-1901) oversaw the height of the **British Empire's global power and influence**, but her reign came long after the **East India Company **had been dissolved and replaced by the British Raj in India.
 
• The **East India Company **was a joint-stock company that was founded in** 1600 and dissolved in 1874,** after centuries of trade and political control in India and other parts of Asia.

questions.question: Who led the Battle of Plassey on behalf of the British East India Company?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Robert clive**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Major-General Robert Clive** was the **first British Governor of the Bengal Presidency**.
 
• He began as a **writer for the East India Company (EIC) who established the military and political supremacy of the EIC by securing a decisive victory at the Battle of Plassey in Bengal.**
 
• The **Battle of Plassey **was fo**ught in north-eastern India on 23 June 1757.** 
 
• **Troops of the British East India Company, led by Robert Clive **, came up against** the forces of Siraj-ud-Daulah, the last Nawab of Bengal, and his French allies.**
 
• The main reason '**'The Battle of Plassey''** took place** when Nawab of Bengal Siraj-ud-Daulah did not like the uncontrolled use of privileges by the East India Company's officials.**
 
 
• **​** Also, **the workers of the company stopped paying the taxes** that became one of the reasons for **the Battle of Plassey.**
 
 

**​** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• **Warren Hastings** was a** British colonial administrator,** who served as **the first Governor of the Presidency of Fort William, the head of the Supreme Council of Bengal, and so the first Governor-General of Bengal in 1772–1785. **
 
 
• Warren Hastings **​**and **Robert Clive **are credited with **laying the foundation of the British Empire in India.**

questions.question: ________ was one of the first Indian rulers to lead an armed rebellion against the British East India Company in 1824 against the implementation of the Doctrine of Lapse.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Kittur Chennamma**__.

__
 
• **The Queen of Kittur, Kittur Chennamma, was one of the first Indian rulers to lead an armed rebellion against the British East India Company in 1824, against the implementation of the Doctrine of Lapse**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Rani Chennamma**, the queen of Kitturu was one such warrior who led a war against British forces in early part of 19th Century when not many rulers were familiar with the evil designs of the British.

 
 
• She was the first Indian ruler to lead an armed rebellion against the British East India Company. 
 
• Chennamma was born in Kakati, a small village in today’s Belagavi district of Karnataka.
 
• She became queen of Kitturu (now in Karnataka) when she married Raja Mallasarja of the Desai family.
 
• They had one son who died in 1824.
 
• After the death of her son, she adopted another child, Shivalingappa, and made him heir to the throne.
 
• However, the British East India Company did not accept this under the Doctrine of Lapse, a policy of annexation devised by the British East India Company.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

The Doctrine of Lapse was a merger policy widely followed by Lord Dalhousie as Governor-General of India from 1848 to 1856. The states that were annexed under this policy are given below in chronological order:

questions.question: After the Battle of Plassey 1757, who from the British East India Company, became Baron of Plassey?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Robert Clive.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Robert Clive:-**

 
 
• He was a British general and statesman who played a key role in the establishment of British rule in India.
 
• He is best known for his victory at the Battle of Plassey in 1757, which gave the British East India Company control of the Bengal Presidency.
 
• **The Baron of Plassey was Robert Clive, 1st Baron Clive of Plassey, (Hence option 1 is correct).**
 
• **Clive served as Governor of Bengal twice, and during his second term he implemented a number of reforms that helped to consolidate British rule.**
 
• He also expanded the British Empire in India by conquering new territories.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Warren Hastings:-**

 
 
• **He was the first Governor-General of Bengal and is considered one of the most controversial figures in British colonial history. **
 
• He was a brilliant administrator and diplomat, but he was also accused of corruption and tyranny.
 
 
 
• **John Laird Mair Lawrence:-**
 
 
• He was an English-born Ulsterman who became a prominent British Imperial statesman.
 
• **He served as the Viceroy of India from 1864 to 1869.**
 
 
 
• **Charles James Napier:-**
 
 
• **He was a British general who is best known for his conquest of the Sindh province in India in 1843. **
 
• During his time as Governor, Napier introduced a number of reforms, including:
 
 
• Abolishing slavery.
 
• Reforming the tax system.
 
• Building new roads and irrigation canals.
 
• Establishing a new judicial system.

questions.question: English East India Company acquired Diwani of Bengal in ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1765**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The English East India Company **acquired the **Diwani of Bengal in 1765 **through the Treaty of Allahabad signed between the Mughal Emperor Shah Alam II and the Company's representative, Robert Clive.
 
• The Diwani of Bengal refers to the right to collect revenue from the Bengal, Bihar, and Orissa regions. This was a significant acquisition for the English East India Company as it gave them control over a vast area and a significant source of revenue.
 
• In 1757, the English East India Company won the Battle of Plassey against the Nawab of Bengal, Siraj-ud-Daulah, which gave them control over Bengal. However, they did not acquire the Diwani until 1765.
 
• While the English East India Company had established its presence in Bengal by this time, they did not acquire the Diwani until 1765.
 
• By this time, the English East India Company had already acquired the Diwani of Bengal and had been collecting revenue from the region for five years.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• From 1600 to 1874, the English East India Company (EIC) operated as a joint-stock business, engaging in trade in the Indian Ocean area.
 
• The company's purpose was to take advantage of trade with India, East and Southeast Asia, and to enable England to trade in East Indian spices.
 
• Later, the EIC acquired and ruled over land, establishing trading factories in India and other Asian countries.
 
• The British Crown annexed the lands of the EIC in the middle of the 19th century and included them in the British Empire.

questions.question: The Charter Act of 1813 extended the East India Company's rule in India to another ________ years.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**20.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Charter Act of 1813 **was passed by the **British Parliament**, which renewed the **East India Company's charter** for another **20 years.**
 
• The Act also allowed** Christian missionaries **to **enter India** for the purpose of** spreading education and knowledge.**
 
• The Act required the East India Company to spend **one lakh rupees** annually on the **promotion of education** in India.
 
• The Act also paved the way for the establishment of the **Hindu College in Calcutta**, which later became the University of Calcutta.
 
• Hence, the correct answer is **option 3.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **East India Company:**

 
 
• East India Company was established in order to** profit from commerce** with **India and East and Southeast Asia.** 
 
• On **December 31, 1600**, it was incorporated by** royal charter.**
 
• In order for England to take part in the** East Indian spice trade**, it was founded as a monopoly commercial organization.

questions.question:
Which of the following statements is correct?

I. Robert Clive had come to Madras from England in 1743 at the age of 18.

II. After the battle of Buxar, the East India Company appointed Residents in Indian states.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Both I and II.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Robert Clive:**

 
 
• At the age of **18, Lord Robert Clive** traveled from **England to Madras in 1743.**
 
• Having triumphed at the **Battle of Plassey in 1757**, he established** Company rule in Bengal.**
 
• **In 1764,** he was chosen to serve as **Bengal's governor.**
 
• The **"Governor-General of Bengal" **was the title given to the governor of **Bengal by the Regulating Act of 1773.**
 
• It is commonly acknowledged that Robert Clive was instrumental in establishing** Bengali British East India Company authority.**
 
 
 
• In Indian states, the Company **installed Residents** following the** Battle of Buxar (1764).**
 
• They were hired as** political or business agents** to represent and advance the **Company's interests.**
 
• The Corporation authorities started meddling in the **internal affairs of Indian states** through the Residents.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Battle of Buxar:

 
 
• The Battle of Buxar took place on** October 22 and 23, 1764.**
 
• It was fought between the forces under the command of the **British East India Company, led by Hector Munro,** and the combined armies of** Mir Qasim, Nawab of Bengal till 1764; the Nawab of Awadh, Shuja-ud-Daula;** and the **Mughal Emperor, Shah Alam II.**
 
• The conflict took place in **Buxar, a "strong fortified town**" in the Bihar region that is situated along the **Gangas river.**
 
• For the** British East India Company**, it was a **difficult win.**
 
• The **Treaty of Allahabad**, which was signed in **1765, p**ut an end to the conflict.​
